clue.text: Insect agitated maid found in pantry running around

indicators.note: found in says the shuffled maid sits inside the turned pantry word
running around tells us to turn the pantry word back to front

parts.note: a pantry or food store is a larder

indicators.note: agitated means the letters of maid are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: A flustered housemaid discovers a bug scuttling about the larder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'agitated' looks like it describes the maid's mood, but it scrambles her name's letters; 'running around' turns the pantry word to REDRAL, and 'found in' houses ADMI there.
explanation.definitionFit: The red admiral is a common butterfly, which is an insect.

clue.text: Lines came up in speech

indicators.note: in speech says the word we want is heard, said out loud, rather than spelt

parts.note: came up means rose, as the sun does

explanation.surface: Some remarks were raised during a talk.
explanation.walkthrough: ROSE ('came up') sounds like ROWS.
explanation.definitionFit: Rows are straight lines of seats or plants, so lines is a synonym.

clue.text: Cover up large herb

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the cover word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a lid is a cover for a pot or box
L is the standard abbreviation for large, as on clothing labels

explanation.surface: Hide a big plant from view.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cover up' reads as hiding something; split, 'Cover' is the lid and 'up' turns it to DIL in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Dill is a feathery herb used with fish and in pickles.

clue.text: Unhappy day with prisoners in quarantine

indicators.note: in places the prisoners word inside the quarantine word

parts.note: to quarantine someone is to isolate them
cons is slang for convicts, that is, prisoners

explanation.surface: A gloomy day spent with inmates locked away in isolation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quarantine' looks like a noun but stands for the verb ISOLATE, which takes CONS after its first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Disconsolate describes someone downcast and beyond comfort, a strong word for sad.

clue.text: Porcelain I damage with edge of implement

parts.note: to mar something is to damage or spoil it

indicators.note: edge of picks out only the opening letter of implement

explanation.surface: Someone confesses to chipping their china with a tool.
explanation.walkthrough: I, then MAR for 'damage', then the first letter of 'implement', I.
explanation.definitionFit: Imari is a style of Japanese export porcelain, named after its shipping port.

clue.text: Attacker using rotten eggs roars

indicators.note: rotten suggests the letters of eggs and roars have gone bad and are rearranged

explanation.surface: A mugger hurls bad eggs and bellows at a victim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rotten' looks like it describes the eggs, but it signals an anagram of EGGS plus ROARS.
explanation.definitionFit: An aggressor is the one who strikes first or starts a fight, an assailant.

clue.text: Goddess aims first to have odd characters removed

indicators.note: removing the odd characters, first, third and so on, keeps only the even letters of aims and first

explanation.surface: A deity sets out her priorities and wants strange people expelled.
explanation.walkthrough: From AIMS keep I and S; from FIRST keep I and S. 'odd characters' reads as weird people but means letters in odd positions.
explanation.definitionFit: Isis was the great mother goddess of ancient Egypt.

clue.text: Marshy areas, small and large, mostly fenced with sticks

indicators.note: fenced with says the large word is enclosed by the sticks word

parts.note: wands are thin rods or sticks

indicators.note: mostly means drop the final letter of the word for large

parts.note: ample means large or plentiful

explanation.surface: Boggy ground of every size, most of it staked off with posts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'small and large' sounds like 'of all sizes', but each word gives letters; 'mostly' leaves AMPL, which 'fenced with' encloses in the sticks.
explanation.definitionFit: Swamplands are tracts of waterlogged ground, the same thing as marshy areas.

clue.text: Big shop certain to contain new poster

indicators.note: to contain says the certain word holds the rearranged letters inside it

parts.note: sure means certain

indicators.note: new tells us poster takes a new form, its letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A large store is bound to display a fresh advertisement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new poster' reads as a fresh advert, but 'new' is the anagram signal giving PERSTO, and 'to contain' sets it inside the certain word.
explanation.definitionFit: A superstore is a very large out-of-town shop or supermarket.

clue.text: Service formerly conveying messages from sources with much energy

parts.note: wells are sources of water, so this is the sources word
far as in far better means much
go means energy or vigour, as in full of go

explanation.surface: An old courier firm drawing on its springs with great vigour.
explanation.walkthrough: Wells Fargo ran stagecoaches and an express and mail service in the American West before becoming a bank.
explanation.definitionFit: The company carried mail and parcels by stagecoach in the nineteenth century, a delivery service of the past.

clue.text: Head of security, in charge, producing file

indicators.note: in places the head of security inside the charge word

parts.note: a rap is a criminal charge, as in a murder rap

indicators.note: Head of takes only the opening letter of security

explanation.surface: The security chief, in command, hands over a document folder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in charge' reads as one phrase meaning in command, but 'in' is the container and 'charge' is RAP, around S. 'file' is the tool, not a folder.
explanation.definitionFit: A rasp is a coarse file for shaping wood or metal.

clue.text: Fighter in joint, not sensible, getting upset with crew

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means the joint and not sensible words together are turned upside down

parts.note: a weld is a joint made by fusing metal
dim means slow-witted, not sensible
an eight is a rowing crew of eight oarsmen

explanation.surface: A boxer in a seedy bar, acting stupidly, gets angry at his team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'joint' suggests a seedy bar and 'upset' anger; in a down entry 'getting upset' flips the joint and dim words together to MIDDLEW. An eight is a rowing crew.
explanation.definitionFit: A middleweight is a boxer in the weight class between welterweight and light heavyweight.

clue.text: Gambler, one enthralled by dancer in racy story

indicators.note: enthralled by means held captive, so the gambler and one sit inside the dancer word

parts.note: a bopper is someone who dances to pop music
a dicer is someone who plays at dice, a gambler
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A punter falls for a nightclub dancer in a steamy tale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'enthralled by' means held captive inside, so the gambler and the Roman one sit within the dancer word.
explanation.definitionFit: A bodice-ripper is a sexually charged historical romance novel, a racy story.

clue.text: Work with power, fantastic verse, is overwhelming

parts.note: op, short for opus, is a musical work
P is the abbreviation for power in physics

indicators.note: fantastic suggests the letters of verse and is are wildly rearranged

explanation.surface: A powerful, fanciful poem is crushing.
explanation.walkthrough: OP and P come first; 'fantastic' turns VERSE plus IS into RESSIVE.
explanation.definitionFit: Oppressive weather or rule bears down heavily, crushing anyone beneath it.

clue.text: Loud group of relations moan endlessly about nothing

parts.note: a clan is a large family group of relations

indicators.note: about says the moan word goes round the nothing
endlessly drops the final letter of the moan word

parts.note: to grouse is to moan or complain
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A noisy family complains on and on about nothing at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' leaves GROUS, and 'about' wraps that round the O for nothing, giving GOROUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Clangorous describes a ringing, clanging din, so it is a word for noisy.

clue.text: Old man tells a tale about woeful defences

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father, one's old man

indicators.note: about says the tale word wraps round the woeful word

parts.note: to lie is to tell a tale, a fib
sad means woeful or sorrowful

explanation.surface: Grandad spins a mournful yarn about fortifications.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like 'concerning' but is the container signal; 'Old man' means father, not grandad.
explanation.definitionFit: Palisades are fences of pointed stakes built as fortifications.

clue.text: Dire end for creature consumed by fish in river

indicators.note: in says the fish word goes inside the river word

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Scotland and another between England and Wales

indicators.note: consumed by means swallowed, so the end letter sits inside the fish word

parts.note: a sprat is a small fish

indicators.note: end for picks out the final letter of creature

explanation.surface: A grim fate for an animal swallowed by a fish in a river.
explanation.walkthrough: Two containers nest: 'consumed by' gives SPERAT, and 'in river' puts that inside the Dee, a British river.
explanation.definitionFit: A desperate situation is grave and urgent, which is what dire means.

clue.text: King stops idiotic plan

indicators.note: stops means plugs a gap, so the king letter goes inside the idiotic word

parts.note: daft means idiotic or silly
R stands for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: The monarch puts an end to a foolish scheme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stops' reads as halting, but it means filling: R goes inside DAFT.
explanation.definitionFit: A draft is a preliminary version or outline, a plan.

clue.text: Material including note referring to kidneys

indicators.note: including says the material word holds the note letter

parts.note: material in the sense of physical, actually existing, means real

explanation.surface: Some cloth with a note attached about kidneys.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Material' looks like cloth but stands for the adjective REAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Renal is the medical adjective for things relating to the kidneys.

clue.text: Give up part, admitting blunder on reflection

indicators.note: admitting means letting in, so the turned blunder word enters the part word

parts.note: to part is to split apart, which is to sunder

indicators.note: on reflection means seen in a mirror, so the blunder word is turned back to front

parts.note: to err is to blunder or make a mistake

explanation.surface: Concede some ground, owning up to a mistake after thinking it over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'part' is the verb, to split; 'on reflection' gives RRE, and 'admitting' lets it in.
explanation.definitionFit: To surrender is to yield or relinquish something, to give it up.

clue.text: Brave editor backing unfashionable man in introduction

indicators.note: backing means coming behind, so the editor letters go at the end
in says the unfashionable and man words go inside the introduction word

parts.note: a start is a beginning, an introduction
out means no longer in fashion
he is the pronoun for a man

explanation.surface: A bold editor supports an old-fashioned fellow in the opening pages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' means supporting, so it places the editor at the back, not a reversal; 'in' puts the unfashionable man inside the introduction.
explanation.definitionFit: Stout-hearted means courageous and resolute, so it is another word for brave.

clue.text: Old-fashioned style in cabaret, romantic

indicators.note: in says the letters run inside the words cabaret and romantic

explanation.surface: A dated look in a sentimental nightclub show.
explanation.walkthrough: The run spans the end of 'cabaret' and the start of 'romantic'.
explanation.definitionFit: Retro means deliberately imitating fashions of the recent past.

clue.text: Projecting piece of metal poker

definitions.meaning: a small metal knob or boss standing out from a surface
... poker is the card game in which some cards are dealt face up

explanation.surface: A protruding metal rod used for stoking the fire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'poker' suggests a fireplace tool, but it is the card game.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a metal knob fixed into a surface and a form of the card game where cards are dealt face up.

clue.text: Nervous for example around director, unknown quantity

indicators.note: around says the example abbreviation wraps round the director letter

parts.note: EG is short for exempli gratia, for example
in algebra x, y and z stand for unknown quantities

explanation.surface: A jittery film director becomes a mystery figure.
explanation.walkthrough: EG goes around D, then Y follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Edgy means tense, on edge, jumpy.

clue.text: One runs acceptable club

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
on means acceptable, as in that's not on

explanation.surface: A single person manages a decent society.
explanation.walkthrough: 'club' is a golf club, not a society.
explanation.definitionFit: An iron is a golf club with a metal head.

clue.text: Told off about wine kept in college

parts.note: C stands for circa, Latin for about
Asti is a sparkling Italian wine
gated is old university slang for confined to college as a punishment

explanation.surface: Scolded over wine drunk in hall.
explanation.walkthrough: At Oxford and Cambridge a student who was 'gated' was confined to college as a punishment.
explanation.definitionFit: To castigate is to rebuke severely, so castigated means scolded.

clue.text: Direction given by brute ignoring bishop

indicators.note: ignoring means leaving out, so the bishop letter is dropped

parts.note: a beast is a brute
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: Orders issued by a savage who pays no heed to the clergy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Direction' reads as an instruction but is a compass point.
explanation.definitionFit: East is one of the four cardinal compass points.

clue.text: Agent led Tory astray according to story

parts.note: a rep, short for representative, is an agent

indicators.note: astray means gone off course, so led and Tory are rearranged

explanation.surface: A political operative misled a Conservative, so the tale goes.
explanation.walkthrough: A Tory is a member of Britain's Conservative Party; 'astray' rearranges the two words to ORTEDLY.
explanation.definitionFit: Reportedly means as people say, by common account.
